NDT training in Fort Worth: how it works for Fort Worth employers and technicians

Short answer: Atlantis NDT delivers ASNT SNT-TC-1A NDT training for Fort Worth employers and technicians at Level I, II and III in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET. Theory runs live online or in arranged classroom sessions; practical training runs onsite at your facility under ASNT Level III oversight. Your employer certifies you against its written practice. Atlantis has no walk-in centre in Fort Worth. Quotes are on request.

Fort Worth is not one NDT market but three. The first is defence and civil aerospace: the fighter plant on the west side of the city, the rotorcraft maker in the mid-cities, and a supplier and MRO network around Alliance and DFW. The second is energy: the Barnett Shale, whose gas gathering, compression and processing infrastructure still wraps around Tarrant, Denton, Johnson, Parker and Wise counties, plus the pipeline and midstream operators whose regional offices sit in the city. The third is heavy industry and transportation: rail (Fort Worth hosts a Class I railroad's headquarters and major yards), structural steel and bridge work across the Metroplex, and the fabrication shops that serve all of the above.

Each of these markets asks for something different. Aerospace primes and Nadcap suppliers qualify to NAS 410 on top of the training base. Pipeline and midstream owners and their contractors work to API 1104 and ASME B31.8 and certify under SNT-TC-1A. Fabricators build to AWS D1.1 and ASME Section VIII. The common thread is ASNT SNT-TC-1A, which is what Atlantis trains to. Request a Fort Worth training quote with your methods, levels and headcount.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Fort Worth

All courses are available to Fort Worth crews as live online theory plus onsite practical, and all course content is reviewed by an ASNT Level III against the SNT-TC-1A body of knowledge. The table maps each method to the Fort Worth work it actually supports.

MethodLevelsWhat Fort Worth employers use it forPrerequisite
Ultrasonic Testing (UT)I, II, III prepPipeline girth welds and wall thickness in Barnett Shale gathering systems; structural welds; rail axles and components; forgings and plate in aerospace supplyNone for Level I; Level I plus documented experience for Level II
Phased Array UT (PAUT)II, III prepEncoded weld inspection on pipeline and pressure equipment; complex geometry scans; replacing film RT on some fabrication jobsUT Level II recommended
Time-of-Flight Diffraction (TOFD)II, III prepThrough-wall sizing on thick welds for vessels and heavy fabrication; often paired with PAUTUT Level II recommended
Radiographic Testing (RT)I, II, III prepPipeline weld radiography to API 1104; castings; CR/DR digital imaging on fabrication and aerospace partsTexas radiographer trainee/certification requirements for anyone handling sources
Magnetic Particle Testing (MT)I, II, III prepWeld toes, lifting equipment, rail components, drill-pipe and oilfield tubulars, structural steelNone for Level I
Liquid Penetrant Testing (PT)I, II, III prepAerospace components and non-ferrous parts; stainless and aluminium weldsNone for Level I
Visual Testing (VT)I, II, III prepWeld visual, structural and bridge inspection, receiving inspection, borescope access checksNone for Level I
Eddy Current Testing (ET)I, II, III prepAircraft structure and fastener-hole inspection in MRO, conductivity checks, heat-exchanger tube testingNone for Level I

A practical way to choose: if you are aiming at energy and pipeline contractors in North Texas, UT and RT (and later PAUT) are the methods that pay back fastest. If you are aiming at aerospace manufacturing or MRO, PT and ET are the usual first methods, with UT for composites and structures later. If you are aiming at fabrication and structural steel, VT, MT and UT make a strong, portable combination. Level III candidates from any of these backgrounds can use ASNT Level III training and exam preparation.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Fort Worth, step by step

SNT-TC-1A is an ASNT recommended practice. It gains force when an employer adopts it in a written practice and when a code or contract such as API 1104, ASME Section VIII or a customer specification refers to it. The path below is the same for a pipeline technician in Fort Worth as anywhere in Texas.

  1. Employer written practice. The employer documents training hours, experience hours, examinations, vision requirements, the Level III responsible for certification, recertification and records. No written practice, no valid certification. See written practice development if yours needs building or updating.
  2. Classroom training hours. The trainee completes method- and level-specific formal training. Recommended minimums are summarised in the training requirements matrix; the written practice may require more.
  3. On-the-job experience. Documented, supervised experience in the method. For field technicians this is typically logged on real pipeline, plant or fabrication jobs.
  4. General examination on method theory and principles.
  5. Specific examination on the employer's procedures, equipment, codes and acceptance criteria, for example API 1104 acceptance standards for a pipeline crew.
  6. Practical examination on real specimens, administered and graded under the authority of a Level III.
  7. Vision test for near-vision acuity and colour contrast, repeated at the interval set by the written practice.
  8. Certification signed by the employer once the file is complete.
  9. Recertification at the interval the written practice sets, by examination or evidence of continued satisfactory performance.

The framework is explained in full at SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Fort Worth crews

We say this plainly on every city page: Atlantis has no training centre in Fort Worth. The delivery model is designed for employers whose crews are spread across the Metroplex and out into the field.

  • Live online theory for classroom hours. Field technicians working rotations across the Barnett or further west can attend without driving into the city. See NDT training online.
  • Onsite practical at your facility. Hands-on sessions at your shop, yard or plant with your equipment, your procedures and specimens that reflect your work: pipe coupons with real weld flaws for a pipeline contractor, machined parts for a manufacturer, structural welds for a fabricator.
  • Classroom cohorts arranged at your site or an agreed venue once a group forms.
  • Corporate programmes that bundle training, examinations, written practice review and Level III services; see corporate NDT training.

For energy employers, timing matters. Gas processing plants and compressor stations schedule maintenance outages, pipeline construction follows project and weather windows, and North Texas summers make midday field work punishing. Theory can run in quieter weeks or evenings, with onsite practical and examinations placed around your job calendar. Ask about onsite training for your Fort Worth crew; cohort and onsite quotes are normally returned within one business day.

Where NDT technicians work in Fort Worth

  • Defence aerospace manufacturing. Lockheed Martin Aeronautics' Fort Worth plant builds the F-35 and F-16, supported by a large supplier base. NDT here is component and structure inspection (PT, ET, UT, RT) under NAS 410 qualification and Nadcap-audited special processes. Naval Air Station Joint Reserve Base Fort Worth shares the airfield.
  • Rotorcraft and business aviation. Bell Textron is headquartered in the Fort Worth area, and the region hosts business-jet service centres and MRO operations around Alliance and DFW. MRO work leans heavily on ET, PT and UT to OEM manuals.
  • Barnett Shale and midstream. Gathering lines, compressor stations, processing plants and transmission pipelines generate UT thickness surveys, weld RT and UT to API 1104, MT/PT on fittings and VT on new construction. Owners generally require SNT-TC-1A certification from contractors, and many operator qualification programmes sit alongside it.
  • Rail. BNSF Railway is headquartered in Fort Worth, and rail yards and car shops across the Metroplex generate UT and MT on wheels, axles, couplers and structural components.
  • Fabrication and structural steel. Metroplex fabricators build skids, vessels, tanks, structural steel and bridge components to AWS D1.1, AWS D1.5, ASME Section VIII and ASME B31.3, with ASME Section V governing NDE methods.
  • Transportation infrastructure. TxDOT's Fort Worth District and local agencies manage steel and concrete bridges across Tarrant County and the surrounding district, with fracture-critical member and weld inspection work going to qualified contractors.
  • Power. Gas-fired generation and utility transmission across North Texas bring boiler tube, piping and structural inspection during outages.

Radiography in Texas. Texas is an NRC Agreement State. Industrial radiography is licensed by the Texas Department of State Health Services (DSHS) Radiation Control Program under 25 TAC §289.255. Texas runs its own industrial radiographer certification: individuals start as trainees with a DSHS trainee status card, complete the required radiation safety course and supervised on-the-job training under an authorised radiographer trainer, and then qualify for certification. This state licensing sits on top of, and is separate from, SNT-TC-1A RT certification by the employer. Atlantis RT method training covers technique, image quality and interpretation; your company's licence, operating and emergency procedures and DSHS requirements govern radiation safety. Check current DSHS rules before planning an RT programme.

What Fort Worth employers typically ask for. Field inspection companies serving North Texas pipelines usually ask for SNT-TC-1A Level II in UT and RT, or UT with MT and VT, plus the owner's safety orientations and operator-qualification tasks where applicable, a driving record suitable for field vehicles, and willingness to travel across the basin. Fabricators ask for VT, MT and UT to AWS D1.1 and ASME acceptance criteria and the ability to read weld symbols and drawings. Aerospace manufacturers and MRO shops ask for PT and ET experience, and will qualify new hires to their NAS 410 or OEM programmes after hire. Rail employers look for UT and MT on wheels, axles and components. The common thread is a clean, documented SNT-TC-1A training and experience record, which lets the employer's Level III build on what the technician already has.

Why Fort Worth crews benefit from onsite practical. The Metroplex is spread out, and field crews are often based at yards on the edge of town or out in the basin. Bringing practical training to the yard, using the crew's own flaw detectors, crawlers or film and digital systems, means technicians practise on the exact equipment and procedures they will be examined on and will use the following week. It also lets the employer's supervisors see how their people perform, which is valuable input for the specific and practical examinations.

For pay expectations, see the NDT salary guide.

Level III services and written practices for Fort Worth NDT companies

The Fort Worth area has many small and mid-sized NDT employers: pipeline inspection contractors, fabrication shops with in-house inspectors, MRO shops and specialist service companies. They share one problem: a written practice and certification system that must survive an owner's audit or a customer's prequalification review, often without a full-time Level III on staff. Atlantis provides:

  • Written practice development and updates for SNT-TC-1A, including adding methods such as PAUT as the business grows. See written practice development.
  • Procedure writing to the codes your customers reference, including API 1104, ASME Section V and AWS D1.1.
  • Examination administration and grading for general, specific and practical exams.
  • Records and audit readiness: training logs, experience hours, vision records and certification files reviewed as an auditor would.

Background on the framework is at SNT-TC-1A training and certification. Book a Level III consultation for your Fort Worth company.

Practise before the practical exam

Trainees can use the Practical NDT 3D simulator to practise 12 methods in 5 environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. For Fort Worth, the aircraft hangar suits aerospace and MRO trainees, while the oil and gas site and welding workshop match pipeline and fabrication work. It builds familiarity with set-ups, scanning and indications. It is practice only and does not replace training hours, supervised experience or the practical examination on real specimens.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. He develops course content, oversees practical sessions and examinations, and works with employers on written practices and Level III services. See all NDT training programmes.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Fort Worth

How do I get NDT certified in Fort Worth?

Under SNT-TC-1A, you are certified by your employer after completing classroom training hours, documented experience, general, specific and practical examinations administered under a Level III, and a vision test. Atlantis provides the training and practical preparation, and for employers, written practices and examinations.

Can I take NDT training online in Texas?

Yes for the theory: classroom hours can be completed through live online sessions. Practical training and the practical examination must be hands-on with real equipment and specimens, which Atlantis delivers onsite at your employer's facility. See NDT training online.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

It depends on the employer's written practice. SNT-TC-1A recommends minimum classroom and experience hours for Level I and Level II, and the experience requirement usually takes the longest. See the training requirements matrix for the recommended figures.

Do I need a license for radiography in Texas?

Yes. Texas is an Agreement State and DSHS licenses industrial radiography under 25 TAC §289.255. Radiographers must hold Texas trainee status and then industrial radiographer certification, alongside their employer's SNT-TC-1A RT certification. Check current DSHS requirements.

What does NDT training cost in Fort Worth?

Quote on request. It depends on methods, levels, number of technicians, onsite practical and any written practice or examination services. Cohort and onsite quotes are normally returned within one business day. Request a Fort Worth quote.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Fort Worth employers?

Yes. SNT-TC-1A is the standard framework for pipeline, midstream, fabrication, rail and structural employers in North Texas. Aerospace primes and Nadcap suppliers generally qualify to NAS 410, which the employer manages on top of the training base.

Does Atlantis offer API 1104 or CWI training?

No. Atlantis training is SNT-TC-1A NDT method training. We teach techniques and acceptance criteria as they appear in the procedures your crews use, including API 1104 pipeline work, but we do not offer CWI, API inspector or NAS 410 certification courses.

Which NDT method is most in demand for Barnett Shale work?

UT (thickness and weld) and RT on pipeline welds are the core methods, with MT, PT and VT on fittings and construction. PAUT is increasingly specified for weld inspection.

Can Atlantis train our crew onsite in Fort Worth?

Yes. Practical training runs at your facility using your equipment and specimens, with theory delivered live online beforehand.

Can Atlantis act as our outside Level III?

Yes. We provide written practices, procedures, examination administration and audit preparation. See written practice development.

Is there a way to practise before hands-on sessions?

Yes, the Practical NDT simulator. It is for practice only and does not replace the practical examination.

Where can I find practice questions?

Start with UT Level 2 practice questions.

Talk to us about NDT training in Fort Worth or see all training programmes.
